bad_plan.subtitle: the day-trader

runs.u: I'm quitting my job tomorrow to day-trade full-time. I've got a system.
runs.reply:
That's a big move, and I'd be doing you a disservice if I just cheered. The honest picture is that the large majority of full-time day traders lose money over a year, and most of the ones who fail also believed they had a system, because a system that looked great in backtests or a strong few months often falls apart under live conditions, slippage, and the pressure of needing it to pay rent.

So a few real questions before tomorrow: how long have you traded this system with real money, and did it survive a genuinely bad stretch? Do you have enough saved to cover a year of living expenses without touching your trading capital, so a drawdown doesn't force you into desperate decisions? And is there a reason it has to be a clean break rather than trading alongside the job for another six months to prove it out with less at stake? If you've got solid answers to those, that changes things a lot. If not, I'd seriously consider waiting.

I'm not saying don't ever do this. I'm saying the downside of waiting a few months to prove it live while employed is small, and the downside of being wrong after you've quit is your savings and a gap on your resume. What's the actual reason it needs to be tomorrow?
